overview: Ambev S.A. is the largest brewer in Latin America and a subsidiary of Anheuser-Busch InBev (AB InBev owns roughly 61-62% of voting/economic interest), listed on the NYSE as ADSs (1 ADS = 1 common share, no par value) and on B3 in Brazil. The company produces, distributes and sells beer, non-alcoholic beverages (NAB, e.g. Guaraná Antarctica, Pepsi under license) and malt across four reporting segments: Brazil (Beer and NAB), Latin America South (LAS: Argentina, Bolivia, Paraguay, Uruguay, Chile), Central America & the Caribbean (CAC), and Canada (Labatt). Brazil is by far the dominant segment, where Ambev holds roughly 55-66% beer market share depending on channel, supported by one of the largest direct-distribution and route-to-market networks in the beverage industry.

business_model.summary: Ambev earns revenue from manufacturing, bottling/canning and selling beer and non-alcoholic beverages, monetized through price/mix (premiumization) and volume across a multi-brand portfolio, increasingly supplemented by take-rate and marketplace revenue from its B2B digital platform BEES and its direct-to-consumer delivery app Zé Delivery. Revenue is substantially transactional/volume-driven (consumer packaged goods), not subscription-based, though BEES marketplace GMV (take-rate economics on third-party products sold to bars/retailers) is building a smaller recurring, asset-light, higher-margin revenue stream on top of core beer/NAB sales. FY2025 consolidated net revenue was R$88.2 billion, down modestly as-reported from R$89.5 billion in FY2024 (BRL appreciation and portfolio/scope effects) but up organically (+3.7% YTD through Q3 2025); normalized EBITDA margin expanded to ~34% in FY2025. 1H2026 showed re-acceleration: net revenue +7.2% organic, normalized EBITDA +9.6% organic with 70bps of margin expansion, aided by NR/hl pricing discipline and a modest return to beer volume growth.

revenue_streams.name: Brazil Beer
revenue_streams.trend: volume soft/declining in 2025 on weather and macro, beer volumes returned to modest growth (+5.0% in Q2 2026) aided by premiumization and World Cup activation

revenue_streams.name: Brazil NAB (non-alcoholic beverages)
revenue_streams.trend: volume declining (-4.4% to -8.6% in recent quarters) while NR/hl (pricing) partially offsets

revenue_streams.name: Latin America South (Argentina, Bolivia, Paraguay, Uruguay, Chile)
revenue_streams.trend: revenue growing organically (+4-9% recent quarters) but heavily distorted by Argentina IAS 29 hyperinflation accounting

revenue_streams.name: Central America & Caribbean (CAC)
revenue_streams.trend: growing organically (+1-7% recent quarters), smallest segment

revenue_streams.name: Canada (Labatt)
revenue_streams.trend: roughly flat to slightly declining volumes, modest NR/hl-driven revenue growth

revenue_streams.name: BEES Marketplace / digital ecosystem (embedded across segments, not separately broken out in revenue)
revenue_streams.trend: GMV growing ~58-120%+ YoY across recent quarters off a small base; increasingly material to gross profit mix and cost/revenue management, not yet a disclosed standalone revenue line

business_model.customer_type: Primarily B2B: hundreds of thousands of bars, restaurants and small retailers (points of sale) served through Ambev's direct distribution network and the BEES ordering/marketplace platform, plus traditional retail/off-trade channels (supermarkets, convenience stores); B2C exposure via Zé Delivery direct-to-consumer app and NAB consumer brands
business_model.geographic_mix: Brazil ~70% of volume and the large majority of EBITDA; approximately 44% of FY2025 consolidated net revenue came from operating companies with non-real functional currencies (LAS, CAC, Canada combined), creating meaningful multi-currency translation exposure on top of commodity-cost dollar linkage

main_competitors: Heineken (Heineken Brazil, ~24-26% Brazil beer market share)
Molson Coors (partner/competitor in Canada via Labatt's market)
competitive_position.market_position: Dominant #1 brewer in Brazil (~55-66% beer market share depending on channel: ~66% on-trade, ~55% retail) and the leading brewer across most of its LAS and CAC footprint; Labatt is a top-2 Canadian brewer. Scale, multi-decade incumbency and AB InBev's global brand portfolio (Budweiser, Corona, Stella Artois, Michelob Ultra) licensed into local markets give Ambev category leadership almost everywhere it operates.

moat_factors.description: One of the most extensive direct beverage-distribution networks in Latin America, reaching hundreds of thousands of points of sale in Brazil alone; replicating this logistics footprint would require years of capital investment, a structural barrier to new entrants and smaller craft players.

moat_factors.factor: Brand portfolio breadth and premiumization capability
moat_factors.description: Multi-tier portfolio spans mainstream (Brahma, Skol, Antarctica), premium/super-premium (Budweiser, Stella Artois, Corona, Original) and the fast-growing 'Balanced Choices' no/low-alcohol segment (Michelob Ultra, Stella Pure Gold, no-alcohol beers), allowing Ambev to capture trade-up spending and defend against craft/import encroachment simultaneously; premium/super-premium brands have been growing high-single to mid-teens even as mainstream volumes soften.

moat_factors.factor: BEES B2B digital platform and data advantage
moat_factors.description: BEES (ordering + marketplace) covers the vast majority of Ambev's Brazil customer base (>90% of active customers purchasing through BEES, >94% of active customers in some disclosures), giving granular, real-time visibility into price elasticity, SKU velocity and customer behavior that smaller competitors lack; BEES Marketplace GMV grew ~58-120%+ YoY in recent quarters, with gross margin on marketplace sales expanding (~22% in 1H2026), turning a cost-saving tool into an incremental, asset-light profit pool.

moat_factors.factor: AB InBev relationship / global scale procurement
moat_factors.description: As AB InBev's Latin American platform, Ambev benefits from global brand licensing, shared procurement scale for inputs (aluminum, barley, hops) and technical/commercial best-practice transfer, though this is also a related-party dependency (AB InBev entities appear extensively in related-party transaction disclosures).

moat_factors.factor: Regulatory/exclusivity arrangements at point of sale
moat_factors.description: Historical exclusive on-trade contracts with bars/restaurants reinforced distribution dominance, though these are now capped (max ~8% of points of sale per state) under a 2023 CADE (Brazilian antitrust) settlement, and Heineken has alleged continued breaches and is pursuing further CADE action — a moat factor now under active regulatory erosion.

weaknesses: Heavy reliance on a single, cyclically and weather-sensitive market (Brazil) for the bulk of profit, with 2025 volumes hurt by unseasonably cold weather in the South/Southeast and weak disposable income in the North/Northeast

Core/mainstream beer segment (the largest volume tier) has been losing volume (low-teens decline in some quarters) even as premium and balanced-choices gain, creating a structural mix-shift execution challenge
Argentina hyperinflation accounting (IAS 29) distorts reported LAS segment economics and complicates like-for-like comparisons for investors
NAB (non-alcoholic beverages ex-beer) in Brazil has been a consistent volume drag, down mid-single to high-single digits in multiple recent quarters
Antitrust/regulatory overhang from Heineken's renewed CADE complaint over alleged continued point-of-sale exclusivity breaches

growth_drivers: BEES platform monetization: Marketplace GMV growth of ~58-120%+ YoY (varying by quarter/market) with expanding gross margin (~22% in 1H2026, up ~670bps YoY), converting a distribution/ordering tool into a growing profit pool; management frames BEES and Zé Delivery as central to the 'digitize and monetize our ecosystem' strategic pillar

Premiumization: premium and super-premium brands (Budweiser, Stella Artois, Corona/Original) have been growing high-single-digit to mid-teens, with Corona/Stella/Original reportedly reaching ~50% share of the premium segment in Brazil for the first time in a decade

'Balanced Choices' / no- and low-alcohol expansion: this sub-portfolio (Michelob Ultra, Stella Pure Gold, no-alcohol beers) grew ~35-65%+ in recent quarters, well ahead of the base business, addressing health-conscious consumers and widening occasions/consumption moments; new launches like Spaten Pro (announced July 2026, a no-alcohol protein beer) extend this pipeline

Revenue management / pricing power: consistent NR/hl (net revenue per hectoliter) growth of 4.6-7.4% in recent quarters has offset volume softness and funded margin expansion even amid commodity (aluminum) cost inflation

Zé Delivery direct-to-consumer growth: monthly active users and GMV growing double digits, used as a brand-trial vehicle (e.g., introducing Michelob Ultra to 250,000+ consumers) and a lens into premiumization/balanced-choices trends ahead of the broader portfolio

Event-driven volume/brand activation: the 2026 FIFA World Cup provided a one-time but meaningful brand-investment and consumption occasion tailwind in Q2 2026 (stepped-up marketing spend, Zé Delivery orders more than doubling on match days)
Continued market share gains in a soft Brazilian industry, as disciplined execution and brand equity allowed Ambev to outperform the overall category even while absolute volumes declined in 2025

business.risk: Persistent volume softness in core Brazil beer and NAB
business.description: Brazil Beer volumes fell -7.7% to -7.9% in Q3 2025 and NAB -8.6%, driven by unseasonable weather and weak disposable income in the North/Northeast; while Q2 2026 showed a return to beer volume growth (+5.0%), NAB and LAS/Canada volumes remained negative that quarter, indicating uneven demand recovery.

Core and core-plus beer segments (the largest volume tier) declined low-teens in some 2025 quarters even as premium and balanced-choices grew; a prolonged shift away from mainstream brands pressures the base of the volume pyramid Ambev's distribution scale depends on.

business.risk: Heineken/CADE antitrust dispute over point-of-sale exclusivity
business.description: Heineken has alleged Ambev continues breaching the 2023 CADE settlement (capping exclusive on-trade contracts at ~8% of points of sale per state) and is pursuing a new complaint; an adverse ruling could further erode Ambev's at-the-bar distribution advantage in Brazil.

Ambev is in the final stages of implementing SAP S/4HANA across Brazilian operations; large ERP migrations carry disruption risk to order fulfillment, financial reporting and customer service during cutover.

financial.risk: Argentina hyperinflation accounting (IAS 29) distorts reported organic growth
financial.description: Since FY2025, Ambev caps Argentina price growth in its organic-growth calculation at a maximum of 2% per month (26.8% annualized) via scope-change adjustments; this methodology change materially affects how LAS segment organic revenue/EBITDA growth is calculated and reported, requiring investors to look past headline organic growth figures to understand underlying volume and currency-adjusted performance in Argentina.

~44% of FY2025 net revenue came from non-real functional-currency operations (LAS, CAC, Canada); the real swung from R$6.19/US$1 (Dec-2024) to R$5.50/US$1 (Dec-2025), an 11.1% appreciation, then to R$5.23/US$1 by Feb-2026 — large translation swings flow directly into consolidated reported results independent of underlying operating performance.

Cash COGS/hl (excluding marketplace) rose 7.4-7.7% YoY in several 2025 quarters, driven by FX and commodity headwinds, particularly aluminum can costs; packaging materials (aluminum, PET) and key inputs (sugar, hops, malt) are dollar-linked, so BRL depreciation directly raises costs even with hedging in place.

financial.risk: Attributable net income affected by NCI and tax-rate volatility
financial.description: Reported profit growth has periodically been flattered or dented by effective tax rate swings (e.g., Q3 2025 normalized profit growth of 7.4% driven by lower income tax rather than operating performance) and by non-controlling-interest treatment; investors should track EBITDA/organic-growth trends rather than headline EPS alone in any given quarter.

regulatory.description: The 2023 CADE settlement already constrains exclusive contracting; a further adverse CADE ruling following Heineken's renewed complaint could impose additional restrictions on Ambev's route-to-market model in Brazil.

regulatory.risk: Data protection and digital platform regulation
regulatory.description: Ambev's BEES, Zé Delivery and TaDa digital platforms process consumer and merchant data subject to Brazil's LGPD and analogous data-protection regimes in Chile, Argentina and Paraguay; expanding ANPD (Brazilian data authority) resolutions increase compliance obligations and enforcement exposure.

As the dominant brewer, Ambev is exposed to potential excise tax increases or alcohol-marketing/advertising restrictions across its Latin American and Canadian markets, a recurring theme in the industry's regulatory landscape though not called out as an immediate pending change in the FY2025 20-F.

The 20-F's forward-looking risk factors explicitly flag developments under the Lula administration's economic and fiscal reform agenda (and, reciprocally, U.S. policy under the Trump administration) as a factor that could affect growth prospects in the Brazilian economy broadly.

macro.description: Beer and NAB volumes are sensitive to disposable income, weather and broader macro sentiment; 2025 industry softness was attributed to 'situational' factors (unseasonable weather, pressure on disposable income, particularly North/Northeast) rather than structural demand destruction, but a sustained macro downturn in Brazil would directly compress Ambev's largest profit pool.

The real has shown double-digit annual swings against the US dollar in recent years (27.9% depreciation in 2024, 11.1% appreciation in 2025); the Argentine peso's hyperinflationary dynamics compound this, both directly (translation) and indirectly (via the IAS 29 restatement mechanics described above).

The 20-F explicitly cites global geopolitical instability, trade/tariff policy and commodity price volatility (aluminum, agricultural inputs) as risk factors that could raise costs or disrupt supply chains across Ambev's footprint.

macro.risk: GLP-1/weight-loss drug adoption as a long-term demand headwind
macro.description: Clinical evidence suggesting GLP-1 drugs reduce alcohol consumption, combined with rapidly growing GLP-1 adoption in Brazil and other Latin American markets, is an early-stage but increasingly discussed structural risk to long-run beer category volumes industry-wide.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: The Brazilian beer market (the world's third-largest by volume) is mature, with per-capita consumption around 70 liters/year and overall market value growth projected in the low-single-digit CAGR range (roughly 1.7-2.3% through the early 2030s) as volume growth plateaus and value growth is driven by premiumization, craft/microbrewery expansion and the rapidly growing no-/low-alcohol segment. 2025 was characterized by industry-wide volume softness in Brazil attributed to weather and disposable-income pressure rather than structural decline; 1H2026 showed a sequential recovery in beer volumes.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate. Beer/NAB are consumer staples-adjacent but have discretionary, weather-sensitive and on-trade (bar/restaurant) demand components that make volumes sensitive to disposable income and seasonal/weather variation, as clearly evidenced by the 2025 volume softness commentary.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low direct sensitivity (no major variable-rate consumer financing exposure), but indirect sensitivity via Brazilian benchmark (Selic) rate effects on consumer disposable income and corporate borrowing costs, and via the relationship between US/Brazil rate differentials and BRL exchange-rate volatility.
key_input_costs: Aluminum (cans) — dollar-linked and a cited driver of recent Cash COGS/hl inflation
Barley, hops, malt and sugar — dollar-linked agricultural inputs
Marketing/sponsorship spend (notably stepped up around major sporting events like the FIFA World Cup)

recent_developments.event: Reported 2Q26 organic net revenue growth of +6.1% and organic Normalized EBITDA growth of +8.9% (margin +80bps to 31.6%); total volumes grew +1.4% with beer volumes up mid-single digits and estimated market share gains, aided by stepped-up brand investment behind the FIFA World Cup. Normalized EPS of R$0.22 grew 24.2% YoY. 1H2026 net revenue grew +7.2% organic and Normalized EBITDA +9.6% organic.

Board approved payment of the final R$1.9 billion tranche of the December-2025-declared Interest on Capital (IOC) distribution (paid October 6, 2026) plus a new ~R$1.1 billion IOC distribution to be paid by December 2026.

Ambev returned approximately R$5.9 billion in cash to shareholders year-to-date, primarily through ~95% completion of the R$2.5 billion share buyback program announced in October 2025, plus 2025 IOC partial payments.
Launched Spaten Pro, a Munich Dunkel-style no-alcohol beer with 10 grams of protein, extending the 'Balanced Choices' innovation pipeline into functional/better-for-you positioning.

BEES Marketplace GMV grew ~58-60% YoY in Q2 2026 and 1H2026 (Brazil marketplace GMV reportedly doubling in 1H2026), with marketplace gross margin expanding ~670bps to ~22%; over 90% of active Brazil customers now purchase through BEES, with ~600+ SKUs offered on the marketplace.

Reported 3Q25 organic net revenue growth of only +1.2% against a -5.8% organic volume decline, offset by +7.4% NR/hl growth; Normalized EBITDA grew +2.9% organically with 50bps of margin expansion. CEO Carlos Lisboa characterized the quarter as one where 'industries softness persisted.' Board approved a new R$2.5 billion (~208 million share) buyback program to be executed over 18 months.

Heineken reportedly prepared a new complaint to Brazil's antitrust regulator CADE alleging Ambev breached the terms of a 2023 settlement that capped Ambev's exclusive point-of-sale contracts at ~8% of points of sale per state, citing fresh evidence from São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro and Brasília.

Ambev amended its organic revenue growth methodology to cap Argentine price growth at a maximum of 2% per month (26.8% annualized) within organic-growth calculations, reflecting the ongoing impact of IAS 29 hyperinflation accounting on the LAS segment; this is a disclosed, recurring methodology adjustment rather than a one-time event.

items.metric: Brazil Beer Cash COGS/hl (excluding marketplace sales of non-Ambev products)
items.notes: Reaffirmed unchanged as of the Q2 2026 release despite a 'dynamic' global geopolitical environment; management explicitly stated it 'maintain[s] our full-year guidance unchanged.' This is the only formal quantitative full-year guidance metric Ambev discloses publicly; the company does not provide formal revenue, EBITDA or EPS guidance ranges.

items.target: Continued IOC distributions and buyback execution
items.notes: R$1.9 billion final IOC tranche (from the December 2025 declaration) paid October 6, 2026, plus a new ~R$1.1 billion IOC distribution to be paid by December 2026. The R$2.5 billion buyback program announced October 2025 was ~95% complete as of the Q2 2026 report, suggesting it will be fully executed within 2026 and a successor program is plausible.

items.target: Continued EBITDA margin expansion via disciplined revenue/cost management
items.notes: Management commentary across 3Q25, Q1 2026 and Q2 2026 releases consistently emphasizes margin expansion (every business unit delivering EBITDA growth and margin expansion in 1H2026) as the central operating target, offsetting FX/commodity cost headwinds (particularly aluminum) through pricing (NR/hl) and cost discipline (Cash SG&A control) rather than through formal numeric EBITDA-margin targets.

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Carlos Lisboa, Q3 2025: 'The third quarter remained dynamic as industries softness persisted. In this context, consistent execution of our strategy strengthened our brands and delivered low-single-digit normalized EBITDA growth with margin expansion.' CEO Carlos Lisboa, Q2 2026: 'The consistent execution of our growth strategy translated into another quarter of beer volume growth, with solid top and bottom-line performance.' Management reiterated in the Q2 2026 release that it remains 'mindful that the global geopolitical environment continues to be dynamic' but is maintaining full-year Brazil Beer Cash COGS/hl guidance unchanged, and continues to frame strategy around three pillars: lead and grow the category (premiumization, balanced choices), digitize and monetize the ecosystem (BEES, Zé Delivery), and optimize the business (cost/revenue discipline).

bull_case: Dominant, hard-to-replicate distribution scale in Brazil (~55-66% beer market share) combined with a multi-tier brand portfolio allows Ambev to keep gaining share even in a soft industry, as demonstrated through 2025's volume downturn

BEES Marketplace is scaling rapidly (GMV growth of 58-120%+ YoY in recent quarters) with expanding gross margins (~22% in 1H2026), representing a genuine, asset-light incremental profit pool layered on top of the core beer business rather than merely a cost-saving tool

Premiumization and 'Balanced Choices' (Michelob Ultra, Stella Pure Gold, no-alcohol beers) are growing far faster than the base business (35-65%+ in various quarters) and align with durable global consumer trends toward moderation and premium experiences, providing a structural growth vector even if mainstream beer volumes stay soft

Consistent pricing power (NR/hl growth of 4.6-7.4% in recent quarters) has repeatedly offset commodity/FX cost inflation and volume softness, evidencing real brand equity and revenue-management discipline rather than reliance on volume growth alone

Strong, growing capital returns to shareholders (R$5.9 billion returned YTD through mid-2026 via buybacks and IOC distributions) funded by robust free cash flow generation, offering a tangible income/return-of-capital component to the thesis independent of multiple re-rating
bear_case: Brazil beer and NAB volumes have been genuinely weak for multiple consecutive quarters (down mid-to-high single digits in 2025), and while management attributes this to 'situational' weather/macro factors, a prolonged or structural Brazilian consumer slowdown would directly compress Ambev's single largest profit pool with no comparable offsetting segment

Argentina hyperinflation accounting under IAS 29 (now capping organic price growth calculations at 2%/month) makes headline LAS segment organic growth figures difficult for investors to interpret cleanly and could mask underlying deterioration or currency-driven distortion in that segment

Renewed Heineken antitrust action at CADE over alleged continued point-of-sale exclusivity breaches creates regulatory overhang that could further erode Ambev's distribution advantage in its most important market

Core/mainstream beer segment — the largest volume tier — continues to lose share to both premium and craft/import alternatives, requiring continuous, costly brand reinvestment to manage the mix shift without further eroding the base

Multi-currency (BRL, ARS and others) translation volatility is structurally embedded in ~44% of consolidated revenue, meaning reported results can diverge meaningfully from underlying organic operating performance in any given year, complicating valuation and creating episodic headline-EPS volatility unrelated to business fundamentals
